Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Iodoquinol may increase the effects of cadexomer iodine through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 9. Iodoquinol may increase the effects of iodinated glycerol through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 10. Iodoquinol may increase the effects of iodine through pharmacodynamic synergy. The clinical significance of this interaction is minor or unknown. 11. Common adverse effects include headache, chills, agitation, diarrhea, rash, fever, urticaria, pruritus, thyroid gland enlargement, retrograde amnesia, nausea, vomiting, peripheral neuropathy, optic neuritis, stomach pain, weakness, visual impairment, optic atrophy, abdominal cramps, and itching of the rectal area. 12. Hypersensitivity to 8-hydroxyquinolones or iodoquinol, as well as iodine sensitivity, are contraindications. Pre-existing optic neuropathy and hepatic damage require caution. 13. Use caution in patients with thyroid disease, as iodoquinol interferes with thyroid function tests for up to six months after discontinuation. 14. Do not repeat the treatment course before 2-3 weeks. Iodoquinol is not effective in treating amebic hepatitis or liver abscess. 15. Avoid long-term therapy due to the risk of optic neuritis and optic atrophy. 16. Pregnancy Category C: The safety of iodoquinol during pregnancy is not established. Lactation safety is unknown. 17. Iodoquinol acts primarily in the intestinal lumen, but its mechanism of action is unknown. Absorption is poor and erratic, metabolism occurs in the liver, and excretion is primarily via feces. 18.
